failure_patterns.pattern: tool_result_persistence: Search calls were left unsaved, or duplicate result-producing calls were made, despite the required assign-and-save workflow.

rejected_edits.content: The same applies when the requested proximity is between hotels and restaurants. Search each requested domain independently; if one lacks required inputs, ask only for those inputs while completing the other ready search. Run `search_nearest` only when results for both sides are available.
rejected_edits.target: A request for a hotel or restaurant “near” a named attraction or landmark is a proximity request: retrieve the attraction results from cache or search for them if absent, then use them with the hotel or restaurant results.

rejected_edits.content: Treat qualitative requests such as “good,” “best,” or “highest-rated” as a ranking preference: sort restaurant results by `rating_restaurants` descending, or hotel results by `rating_hotels` descending when applicable, and save the sorted result. Do not invent a numeric rating threshold.
rejected_edits.target: For ratings, treat a single numeric rating without minimum or “at least” language as exact `[x, x]`; “exactly x” is `[x, x]`, and an explicit “at least x” request is `[x, 5]`.

rejected_edits.content: - For a one-sided flight-time bound, complete the range to the day boundary: “by” or “before X” uses `["12:00 AM", X]`, and “after X” uses `[X, "11:59 PM"]`, preserving the stated AM/PM value. Apply this to both `departure_time` and `arrival_time`.
rejected_edits.target: - For a one-sided flight-time bound, complete the range to the day boundary: “before X” uses `["12:00 AM", X]`, and “after X” uses `[X, "11:59 PM"]`, preserving the stated AM/PM value.
